verdict.rationale: Luma documents its own video generation API: a generation endpoint, Python/JS/TS SDKs, agent-readable docs (llms.txt and .md versions of doc pages), and a published credit price table, so an agent could plausibly submit a prompt and estimate cost from the docs. The evidence never shows job-status polling, asset download, or a per-job cost readout, and no OpenAPI spec could be found. missing for 10: documented job status/polling or callback flow, documented asset retrieval, per-generation cost or credit reporting via the API, machine-readable OpenAPI spec, hands-on corroboration of an end-to-end agent loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can run the full video loop from docs alone: submit the prompt, watch the job, fetch the asset, and report the cost

citations.quote: Two endpoints, Python/JS/TS SDKs, credit-based pricing
Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.
